content:
Answers to scan_project's five standing open_questions, synthesized from the existing README/.ai/docs (not a fresh human interview — the answers were already implicit in prior documentation, just never captured under these exact headings):

1. Primary purpose / business problem: AI coding agents (and humans) working in a codebase routinely lack reliable, current context — READMEs go stale, tribal knowledge lives in people's heads, and hand-maintained docs drift from what the code actually does. This project solves that by mechanically scanning a repo, asking a human the things only a human can answer (purpose, users, constraints) instead of guessing, and maintaining living `.ai/docs` (human-facing) + `.ai/context` (agent-facing) built from an append-only evidence archive, so every documented fact is traceable back to its source and re-synthesizable when it drifts.

2. Target users / stakeholders: (a) developers/teams who want reliable AI-agent context for their own codebase, used directly via any MCP client (Claude Code, Gemini CLI); (b) the author (davindermahal), dogfooding it on this repo itself as the primary real-world usage so far; (c) downstream, `ai-intake-mcp` (a separate Jira ticket-execution harness) as a planned future consumer that would read `.ai/context/` during planning and call `record_evidence` during implementation, once that integration is built.

3. Definition of done / success criteria: No single "done" — this is an ongoing tool, not a one-shot deliverable. Success per release milestone is defined in `.ai/docs/project-context.md`'s "Current status" section (kept current there, not duplicated here): currently Phase 1 + Phase 2 complete, plans lifecycle shipped, both packages published to npm at 0.1.1, CI green. Per-onboarding-run success: a caller can run `start_documentation` once and get accurate, evidence-traceable docs without memorizing tool call order, and later detect staleness via `check_drift` (code-vs-scan) and `needs_resync` (evidence-vs-docs).

4. Hard constraints: no compliance/performance/security constraints beyond this being a local, stdio-transport dev tool (not a service handling end-user data). The real hard constraints are architectural invariants: never write or touch `.ai/intake-mcp.json` (owned exclusively by `ai-intake-mcp`); evidence entries are append-only and never rewritten in place; the `.ai/` file layout must never drift between this server and `ai-intake-mcp`, enforced by both depending on the same `@davindermahal/context-schema` package rather than duplicating types; any migration of pre-existing/foreign `.ai/` content must be non-destructive (copy-first — originals kept unless `remove_originals` is explicitly set).

5. Deployment: no infrastructure at all — both packages are published to npm (`@davindermahal/context-schema`, `@davindermahal/documentation-mcp`) and run as a local stdio-transport MCP server subprocess, launched by an MCP client's config (`npx -y @davindermahal/documentation-mcp`). No servers, containers, or cloud infra to deploy; CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) only builds+tests on push/PR to `main`, it doesn't deploy anything.
